summary: Parse positional numeric arguments with strconv.Atoi instead of fmt.Sscanf("%d"), and name the portal's amended-text suffix when an argument carries one.
reason: Sscanf("%d") reads the leading digits and discards the rest without an error, so every command taking <legisl> <numero> silently accepted a trailing suffix and answered about a different document: `ddl stralci 18 1030/A` became 1030, and `ddl get 18 1030/A` opened ddl 1030 while claiming to have opened what was asked. The `N/A` form is not a typo - it is how the portal's committee summaries and the press cite the amended text of a bill - so it reaches the CLI from anyone starting out from a news story. Rejecting it with a message that names the base number is the only reading that neither guesses nor hides the reinterpretation. `ddl stralci` is the one declared exception: there the family of split-off bills genuinely is the same for 1030 and 1030/A, so the suffix is accepted and the report says in `note` why the answer coincides with the bare number, and `--dry-run` says the same.
validated_outcome: `ddl get 18 1030/A` now exits with `argomento "numero" non valido: 1030/A. Il suffisso "/A" indica il testo emendato, ma l'archivio indicizza per numero base: ripeti con 1030` instead of returning ddl 1030; `ddl stralci 18 1030/A` returns the same nine split-off bills as `18 1030` plus a note explaining why, and `ddl stralci 18 6030/A` (a base with no split-offs) keeps both the suffix note and the empty-result note. TestAtoiArgRifiutaLaCoda and TestNumeroConSuffisso cover the parse; `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.
